prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: Cc1ccnc2c1NC(=O)c1cccnc1N2C1CC1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL247

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV1 wild-type reverse transcriptase using [3H]dTTP by scintillation counting
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of wild type HIV1 reverse transcriptase using oligo(dT)16 as primer measured after 40 mins by picogreen-dye based spectrofluorimetric analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against wild-type HIV-1 reverse transcriptase in a cell-free enzymatic inhibition format with confidence score 9, and while the detection methods differ (scintillation counting vs. picogreen spectrofluorimetry), the underlying biochemical reaction (DNA polymerization by RT) is the same, so results are expected to be reasonably concordant."}

parsed.reason: Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against wild-type HIV-1 reverse transcriptase in a cell-free enzymatic inhibition format with confidence score 9, and while the detection methods differ (scintillation counting vs. picogreen spectrofluorimetry), the underlying biochemical reaction (DNA polymerization by RT) is the same, so results are expected to be reasonably concordant.
